- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price drops, model underreacts; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast to avoid underestimation.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 65–70 range, model tends to overcorrect; adjust forecast toward historical mean (67–69) for next 2–3 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates long-term upward trends; add 1–2% cumulative bias toward higher end of range if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model misreads momentum; use weighted average of recent 3–5 sentiment values to adjust forecast direction.
